what: NEXT-2's survey (survey_next2.sh) on the committed tree, which placed GP-LANES and recorded what else the step has: peak -- fma_peak.c, 24 independent AVX-512 FMA chains in registers, GFLOP/s a thread on 1, 2, 4 threads; ceiling -- gemm_ceiling.c, the T256 step's GEMM shapes (k-blocked, four threads), each thread its own operands back to back (the kernel's all-core ceiling) against one thread and the pool's one GEMM, median of 11 rounds of 200 calls, twice; jobs -- gemm_jobs.c, the step's GEMM jobs at T256 as the trainer issues them against four threads each running the whole job on its own operands, median of 11 rounds of 200 jobs, twice; pool_rtt -- pool_rtt.c, 2,000 jobs of trivial tasks back to back and after a pause; probe -- probe_jobs.py's copies in a worktree of the tree, probe_step.py: every pool job of the GEO step by its launch's claim (T256 split by task count), its wall time, its workers' entry, busy share and finish; order -- probe_order.py, one T256 step's jobs in order; not_taken -- GROUP-ROWS-0 (proto_group_rows.py) and COMMIT-BLOCKS-0 (the update's commit in chunks of 16,384, the tree's 65,536): ../pool-affinity/step_one.c, one library a process, alternating, six runs each, every run's weights the same digest, and the commit job itself by probe_step.py (two runs a chunking, alternating); rope -- rope_bench.c (ROPE-TABLE-0), bcir_tensor_rope_pool against the rotation reading a table of the same cosines and sines, 8 calls each way compared byte for byte, then the median of 9 rounds of 100 calls, B4, 4 heads of 32, clang and gcc
